title: Scale Scout
tags: ratios,proportional relationships,constant of proportionality,unit rate,steady pace,tables,graphs,origin,scale,scale drawing,map scale,maps,area,percent,percent change,percent increase,percent decrease,percent error,seventh grade,grade 7,middle school,math,maths,3d,village,survey,read aloud,learning
description: A survey camp outside a village in the morning, and a paper map on a board. Three walkers each left a table of hours and kilometers: whose distance is proportional to the time? Find the kilometers for 1 hour from a table and from a graph. Then use the map: 1 centimeter is 250 meters, the mill is 6 centimeters away, so how far is the walk? Put a pin where the tower goes, find a field's real area, and redraw a wall at a new scale. Last, the percent report: the tank dropped from 80 liters to 60, and the survey said 48 meters where 50 is true. Plan an answer, run it, and see what it really gives. Every instruction is read aloud.
notes: Number Quest Unit 4 of the grades 6-8 street, The Map Room (grade 7): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.2.0 in the Medieval Village theme 1.1.0 in the morning (ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/scale-scout.test.js checks the literal map). The village (hexagon ground, windmill, watermill, tower, church, houses, farm fields, trees, hills) is the theme's own pieces and the flags are its blue flag; the survey line (a plank with six pegs) and the board's posts are the game's own simple meshes. The tables, the double number line, the graphs, the map with its ruler, the field plan and the bars are drawn by the game on one paper board that always faces the player. Three chapters of six rounds (lesson mode: chapter=constant|scale|percent and lock=1): Steady Pace (4.1: which table is proportional, the constant from a table and from a graph, a unit rate from two fractions, which graph is proportional, a steady pace used for more hours), Map and Ground (4.2: from the map to the ground and back, the scale as the equation d = 250c, a real area from a plan, a wall drawn again at another scale, the scale as the point (1, r) of a graph) and Percent Report (4.3: percent drop and increase, percent error, the amount after a percent change, the amount before one, and a two-step route problem). Plan first, then run: a stepper with a Run button, or three tiles; a pin on the map and a wall on the new plan are drawn as they are set, any other number stays on the stepper until it is run; a wrong plan is run and drawn as it really turns out (the walk stops short of the mill, the tank ends at another level), with a spoken hint, and the round stays open. Contexts are walks, maps, a water tank, sacks of grain and measurement error: nothing is priced, bought or sold. No timer, no lives, no fail state, nothing typed, no reward currency. Read-aloud is on by default (BRB.speak, friendly voice): lines are written the way they are said. Keys: arrows or + and - move the stepper (a held button repeats), Enter runs, 1 to 3 pick a tile. Each right round plants a flag on the survey line, and the sixth reports game over (won) once, which completes the course step. Saves only which chapters are finished. English only.
